## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tissopianusayakathā* (Kv 11.1) is a debate located in the *Kathāvatthu* of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The controversy examined in this text concerns the status of latent dispositions (*anusaya*) [Waldron 2003]. According to secondary analysis, non-Theravādin interlocutors—specifically identified as the Sammatīyas and the Mahāsaṅghikas—asserted that latent dispositions are karmically indeterminate or neutral (*anusayā abyākatā*), which would permit them to coexist with skillful (*kusala*) or neutral states of consciousness (*citta*) [Waldron 2003]. Theravādin orthodoxy challenges this stance by arguing that latent dispositions are not distinct from manifest afflictions, pressing the dilemma that if dispositions were considered dissociated from consciousness, active manifest afflictions would likewise have to be dissociated from mind, an implication rejected by both disputants [Waldron 2003].

While SuttaCentral notes no curated external parallels, it records one translation in a modern language [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports extensive Pali-internal text reuse comprising 994 matches across 51 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual alignments within the *Kathāvatthu* occur with other debates on dispositions and mental factors, including the *Anusayāanārammaṇātikathā* (Kv 9.4), *Ñāṇaṁcittavippayuttantikathā* (Kv 11.3), and *Aññoanusayotikathā* (Kv 14.5), as well as treatises from the *Yamaka* (e.g., *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa*, *Pariññāvāra*, *Sānusayavāra*), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* (*Dukanikkhepa*), and the commentary *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-tradition DharmaNexus machine matches align segments of the text with Tibetan translations of Indian Abhidharma works, primarily the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā Lakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093) and the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4091) [DharmaNexus].
